b: I've seen outdoor ads where you almost need to pull over to read everything on them.
A headline, subheading, three selling points, a website, two phone numbers and a QR code. All that for someone driving past at 60 km/h. I understand the thinking.
When you're paying for advertising space, you want to make the most of it. But sometimes, trying to say everything means people remember nothing.
I'm actually interested in how others in the industry handle this. When a client wants to squeeze more information onto a billboard, how do you convince them that less might actually work better?
